title: Rav Huna of Barnish

paragraphs: At [Shabbat 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.28a.7-8), Hyman cites Yuchasin and Dikdukei Soferim for the name Rav Huna of Barnish in connection with an objection to Rav Ashi. Hyman’s own text reads Rava of Barnish.[^2]

notes.text: The Barnish occurrence in the supplied Shabbat 25a citation remains unlocated in the returned research. No matching named passage is supplied for it, and no whole-folio or work-wide absence is asserted. The Huna/Rava alternatives remain Hyman’s reported readings.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. I, pp. 357–358) cites Shabbat 28a. The supplied Hebrew gives 25a. The linked Bavli has Rava of Barnish twice, with the second statement continuing on [28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.28b.1). [Dikdukei Soferim, Shabbat p. 52, note mem](https://books.google.com/books?id=hF923F9uFWAC&pg=PA52) records Ravina in the first position and Rav Huna in the second in its manuscript column. The [1857 Yuchasin, p. 126](https://www.daat.ac.il/daat/vl/yohasin-zakut/yohasin-zakut08.pdf#page=30) gives Huna with Rava as a variant. Heilprin has entries under [Rav Huna of Barnish](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=996&lang=en) and [Rava of Barnish](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3090&lang=en).
